chunks: Al-Ridha, Ali ibn Musa عليه السلام, wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in what he wrote as a response to his questions:

The reason for salat (prayer) is that it is an acknowledgment of the Lordship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a casting off of rivals, and a standing before the Compeller, exalted is His majesty, with humility, lowliness, submissiveness, confession, and seeking reprieve from previous sins, and the placing of the face upon the earth every day in magnification of Allah, exalted is His majesty.

And so that he may be remembering, not forgetful nor insolent, and be humble, abased, desirous, seeking increase in religion and in worldly life, along with what is in it of obligation and persistence in the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by night and day.

So that the servant does not forget his Master, his Regulator, and his Creator, and thus become insolent and transgress; and that this, in his remembrance of his Lord, Mighty and Exalted, and his standing before Him, may be a restraint for him from acts of disobedience and a prevention for him from the various kinds of corruption.

key_terms.الذُّلِّ: humble lowliness before Allah in worship
key_terms.الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ: Lordship; Allah’s sovereign nurturing and authority acknowledged in prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the prescribed act of worship being explained
key_terms.الْأَنْدَادِ: rivals or equals set up besides Allah, which prayer rejects
key_terms.الْإِقَالَةِ: reprieve or pardon sought from past sins
key_terms.الْخُضُوعِ: submissiveness and inward humility in prayer
key_terms.الْمَعَاصِي: acts of disobedience from which prayer restrains a person
key_terms.ذِكْرِ: remembrance of Allah maintained through prayer

ai.seo_question: Why was salat (prayer) made obligatory according to Imam al-Ridha عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that salat (prayer) is prescribed as an affirmation of Allah’s Lordship and a rejection of all rivals besides Him. It cultivates humility, remembrance, and seeking forgiveness, while also protecting the servant from forgetfulness, sin, and corruption through constant standing before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.645 - Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in response to his questions, saying:

"The reason for the prescription of prayer is that it is an acknowledgment of Allah’s (swt) Lord (azj)ship, a rejection of idols, and a standing in the presence of the Mighty, the Glorious, with humility, poverty, submissiveness, confession, and a request for the forgiveness of past sins. It involves placing one's face on the ground daily as an act of magnifying and glorifying Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic.

The prayer ensures that one remains mindful, not forgetful or arrogant. It makes one humble, submissive, desirous, and seeking an increase in faith and worldly needs, in addition to making it obligatory and continuous remembrance of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, by day and night

so that the servant does not forget his Lord (azj), Master, and Creator, and thus does not become boastful or overstep limits. Standing in prayer serves as a deterrent against sins and a barrier from engaging in corruption."
